content:
New Model Focused on Fast Inference

OpenAI announced GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, a lighter and faster version of its agentic coding model, GPT-5.3-Codex. The company stated that it has optimized this new model for development processes requiring rapid iteration and real-time collaboration.

Cerebras Wafer Scale Engine 3 Integration

The model’s infrastructure utilizes Wafer Scale Engine 3 (WSE-3) chips from OpenAI’s hardware partner, Cerebras. Equipped with 4 trillion transistors, these chips are designed to support workflows that require extremely low latency. This move stands out as a concrete example of OpenAI’s strategy to diversify its infrastructure—currently dominated by Nvidia—by working with manufacturers such as Cerebras, AMD, and Broadcom.

Technical Specifications and Performance

Although GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark performs slightly worse than the base model, GPT-5.3-Codex, in complex software engineering tasks, it offers an advantage in terms of speed. While the model lags behind in SWE-Bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0 tests, it aims to maintain developers’ creative flow by generating over 1,000 tokens per second.

  • Context Window: 128,000 tokens.
  • Data Type: Text-only support.
  • Access: Research preview in the Codex app and limited API access for ChatGPT Pro users.

Cerebras CTO Sean Lie emphasizes that this model is a starting point for exploring new interaction models made possible by fast inference.
